text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA

- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic says the essence of the conflict in the Bosnian Serb republic is whether the rule of law will be established or crime will be allowed to flourish, in her response to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic reiterated accusations against the republic's government and state bodies of being tightly linked to criminal dealings.
- Serbian parliament to discuss draft law on election units, which proposes raising number of units from nine to 29.
- Yugoslavia's six month trade deficit is $1.08 billion, according to statistics.
- Czech chemical processing factory Bohemia interested in purchasing 51 percent stake in Serbia's chemical factory Slavica.
- International mediator for the succession of former Yugoslavia Sir Arthur Watts has arrived in Belgrade to meet the Yugoslav side on a tour of bilateral talks with ex-Yugoslav republics

- Bosnian cardinal Vinko Puljic and Serbian Patriarch Pavle agreed in Belgrade to form and inter-religious council in Bosnia which would group the Roman Catholic church, the Serbian Orthodox church, the Islamic religious community and the Jewish community.
- A Yugoslav soldier was injured on the Yugoslav-Albanian border in a clash between a border patrol and a group of Albanians who tried to cross illegally into Yugoslavia.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslavia and Croatia to sign six inter-state agreements during Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic's visit to Belgrade in mid-July.
- Yugoslav Left (JUL) expressed concern over developments in Bosnian Serb republic and warned internal disputes and fight for personal positions should not be allowed to lead to losing land.
BORBA

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and Serb member of Bosnian collective presidency Momcilo Krajisnik agree in talks in Belgrade that crisis in the Bosnian Serb Republic can be resolved only through cooperation of state and political institutions.
- Accounting and Payments office opens account for Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency through which farmers will be paid for this year's wheat crop in cash and commercial paper.
- Yugoslav ambassador to Croatia Veljko Knezevic says new authorities in the eastern Slavonia region are not functioning well.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Slovenia does not recognize new Yugoslav blue passports, visas issued only in old red passports, Yugoslav travel agencies say.

- No official reports from Yugoslav parliament yet on who is in the race for the post of federal president. Nominations can be submitted up to 48 hours before next parliament session, set for July 15.

- Trial of three ethnic Albanians on charges of terrorism continues in Pristina District Court. After admitting to crimes before the court on June 3, prime defendant Besim Rama rescinds his statement. Twelve more Albanians being tried in absentia.
- Kraljevo wagon factory concludes deal for production of 402 wagons for Burma worth $11 million.

- Yugoslavia has not used most of the trade preferentials for exports to the European Union. Of the approved quotas, only 520 hectolitres of plum brandy and a third of the planned 1,500 tonnes of tobacco exported. Food is not a trump card since the EU doesn't know what to do with it either, says Petar Stankovic of the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce.
- One third of the 3,500 invalids of the 1991-95 wars on territory of former Yugoslvaia without housing.
- From August 1, import duties on cars up to 1,500 cc 40 percent, above that 35 percent. Official car dealers sold just 2,400 imported cars in the first five months of the year.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Slovenian businessmen more and more frequently restoring old ties with Yugoslav partners.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --

- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic says it is the police's fault if Bosnian Serb general Ratko Mladic is indeed in Montenegro and that the general is not welcome in Yugoslavia and Montenegro as long are there is doubt he has committed war crimes.
- Pro-Monte GSM mobile phone company has 8,500 subscribers after one year in operation. The company plans to have 12,000 subscribers this year.
- The humanitarian agency Swiss Disaster Relief (SDR) has built 24 flats for refugees in Niksic and will restore the Kotor psychiatric hospital and other facilities in Podgorica.
- The Democratic Union of Albanians will not interfere in relations between Montenegrins and Serbs said the DUA president Ferhat Dinosa. -- Belgrade newsroom 381 11 311 4305
